content.rationale:
This decision is prose because the commitment is a policy about what a failure leaves of work already done and what a second invocation may do — a relation among an attempt, a failure and a retry, not a stored artifact or a single requirement sentence. Its gate is review-criteria and nothing runs: a reviewer reads the clauses against the six recorded prerequisites.

Both answers are this node's own and are written as such. nwswzlnw fixes where the commit sits and what the store holds after a failure before it; it says in terms that it fixes the store and not an order of undo, and the three acts — the abandonment of the draft's change, the forget of its workspace and the removal of its directory — lie outside the store (vxltqruo, vzposmvm). So no-rollback is not the commit point's consequence, and the content states it as this node's answer. The same holds for the retry: vzposmvm tolerates an absence at the two crossings of one discard, and vxltqruo reaches no change when the workspace is gone, but both are answers inside a single discard; whether a second invocation is admitted at all is left open, and the content answers it here rather than reading it out of either. The two limbs are kept apart for that reason: (a) is stated as this node's own because nothing records what a failure leaves of completed acts, and (c) is stated as this node's own because nothing records whether a later invocation proceeds.

The record clause is the one thing that is not new, and the content says so. That a named draft's record remains and the draft is still open is the commit point read after a failure: with the removal untaken, no record has left and every named draft is still an open draft (nwswzlnw, tvxspkyy). Stating it as that consequence, and only that far, keeps it from settling what a failure before the commit leaves in the store, which is nwswzlnw's.

The two answers are one commitment. No rollback without a retry that proceeds would leave a half-ended draft that no invocation could finish without a repair of jj's state, which a discard is not (tvxspkyy); a retry without no-rollback would undo the work it then repeats. Held together they say one thing about a failure before the commit: the completed acts stand, the draft stays open, and the same discard may be asked again and reaches the commit. That is also why the record matters here and not only the acts — because the draft is still open (nwswzlnw), the second invocation is the same discard of the same draft (tvxspkyy), not a new draft and not a different act.

The prerequisites are used by scope, not restated. Which change is abandoned and its empty case stay vxltqruo's and ywsulkzu's, and the requirement form of the change half stays ywsulkzu's; the forget, the directory removal, their order and the per-crossing tolerance stay vzposmvm's, and the requirement form of the workspace half stays ovmqxwuk's; a drifted draft being discardable, and a discard not being a repair, stay tvxspkyy's. The content names those boundaries where a reader might otherwise expect this node to have moved them, especially at a cleared part, where the retry answer deliberately admits the invocation without saying what the abandonment, the forget or the removal does there.

Deliberately not here, because each can be decided, changed or dropped without moving whether a failure rolls back or whether a re-run proceeds: the verb surface — the command, its name, flags and arguments — and the output, refusal wording, stream and exit status, including how a failure of an act or of the removal reaches the user; the exact jj invocations and flags behind the acts; the mechanism, atomicity, durability and concurrent-writer behaviour of the registry write; and the record's field set or serialization. Each belongs to a commitment recorded or planned elsewhere.
content.content:
A discard that fails before its commit leaves the acts it has already completed standing, and a second invocation of the same discard goes on through what is already clear to the commit instead of refusing. Those are this node's two answers: what becomes of the work a failed discard finished, and what a re-run finds. They are written here as this node's own, because no prerequisite states either. nwswzlnw fixes where the commit sits and what the store holds after a failure before it, and expressly leaves an order of undo outside itself; the acts in question lie outside the store, so that node neither answers for them nor forbids an answer. The tolerances recorded elsewhere are tolerances inside one discard, asked at that discard's own crossings (vzposmvm, vxltqruo); whether a later invocation proceeds is not among them. So the no-rollback answer and the retry answer are stated here, and nothing attributes them to a prerequisite.

The acts a failed discard completed are not rolled back. A failure can fall after part of the draft's work has gone through and before the commit, and when it does, what went through stays: a change already abandoned by that invocation is left abandoned, a workspace already forgotten by it is left forgotten, and a directory already removed by it is left removed. Nothing compensates for them. The invocation that failed writes no undo of its own work — it does not re-create the workspace it forgot, re-create the directory it removed, or restore the change it abandoned, and it hands none of them to undo or redo to step back, because a discard is not one of the three operations and offers the history no unit (tvxspkyy). The forget and the directory removal write no registry record, no node, no change and no marker (vzposmvm, tvxspkyy), and the abandonment is no more a registry write than they are; none of the three is an operation that undo or redo could step (tvxspkyy). So there is nothing in the registry or the graph for a compensating write to reach even if one were intended. A half-ended draft is what a failure before the commit leaves on the acts' side: the change given up, the workspace given up, the tree cleared, and all of it left as the failed attempt made it.

Because the commit has not happened, every named draft's record remains and every named draft is still open. That is nwswzlnw's commit point read after a failure rather than a second outcome: the removal is the commit, a failure before it has taken no record, so each named draft's document is still at its handle and each named draft is still an open draft the registry holds (nwswzlnw, tvxspkyy). This is what the no-rollback answer needs in order to be usable. A draft whose change, workspace and directory are already gone is still an open draft — exactly as a draft whose workspace jj no longer has is still an open draft (tvxspkyy, vzposmvm) — so the failed attempt has not ended it, the record is still there to be ended, and the end remains a discard's business.

A re-run proceeds through an already-cleared part and reaches the commit. A second invocation of the same discard finds the completed acts still standing (no rollback, above) and the record still open, so it is a discard of the same open draft and not a new one (tvxspkyy, nwswzlnw), and it goes through what is already clear rather than refusing because it is clear: an already-abandoned change does not stop it, an already-forgotten workspace does not stop it, and an already-removed directory does not stop it. It performs the parts still to be done and reaches the removal. A clear part is not a failure and is not treated as one; the invocation is refused for nothing the first attempt had already completed. What a second attempt cannot complete is a failure like any other and falls under nwswzlnw's rule, unchanged.

What the re-run's acts do at a cleared part is not settled here, and the retry answer does not depend on it. Which change the abandonment reaches, and that none is reached when the workspace is gone, are vxltqruo's and ywsulkzu's, and the requirement form of that half is ywsulkzu's. The forget and the removal of the directory, their order and the tolerance of an absence at either crossing within one discard are vzposmvm's, and the requirement form of that half is ovmqxwuk's. This node admits the second invocation through a part those nodes already make clear; it does not say what the abandonment, the forget or the removal does there, and it moves none of those rules.

These two answers are one commitment, not two policies. The no-rollback answer says the completed work stays; the retry answer says the next invocation goes on from it. Either alone would force the other to be wrong: with no rollback but a refusal on a clear part, the draft would be stuck half-ended with no invocation able to finish it, and the only way out would be a repair of jj's state that a discard is not (tvxspkyy); with a retry that went through clear parts but a rollback first, the retry would have nothing to go through and the completed work would be undone and redone for no gain. Held together they say one thing: a failure before the commit leaves the draft half-ended and still open, and the same discard may be asked again and will finish it.

Not settled here. Where the commit point sits and what a failure before it leaves in the store are nwswzlnw's, and the record remaining above is that answer read after a failure, not a restatement of it. The forget-then-directory order and the tolerance of an absence at either crossing are vzposmvm's. Which change is abandoned, and that none is abandoned when the workspace is gone, are vxltqruo's and ywsulkzu's. The verb surface — the command, its name, flags and arguments — and the output, refusal wording, stream and exit status, including how a failure of an act or of the removal reaches the user, are not settled here. Nor are the exact jj invocations and flags behind the acts, the mechanism, atomicity, durability or concurrent-writer behaviour of the registry write, or the record's field set or serialization. This node answers only what a failure before the commit leaves of the acts it completed and what a second invocation finds.
